mechanism: Caffeine inhibits CYP1A2 which metabolizes amitriptyline, and both drugs have additive CNS and anticholinergic effects; caffeine also increases sympathomimetic stimulation which may antagonize amitriptyline's sedating effects.
action: Counsel patients to limit caffeine intake; monitor for increased amitriptyline side effects (anticholinergic, cardiac arrhythmias) and reduced therapeutic sedation; consider dose adjustment if excessive caffeine consumption occurs.
